# Lienzo Help

The pages of Help in the app (menu → Help, ⌘K, or the ? in the Properties panel). Agents read the same pages with `canvas_catalog help`. Shortcuts are the defaults, as on a Mac; Ctrl replaces ⌘ elsewhere.

## Start here

### What Lienzo is

A canvas next to your agent, where it draws what it explains.

Lienzo (Spanish for canvas) is a canvas that lives next to your agent. The agent draws what it explains as cards, links and Frames while you talk to it in your own chat. You can draw on it too, rearrange it, and point at things to ask about them. Each document is also called a Lienzo; they are kept on this computer and listed in Lienzos.

#### By hand

1. Open Lienzos from the title at the top, or from the menu.
2. Press New Lienzo, or pick one to open.
3. Draw with the toolbar at the bottom, or ask your agent to draw.

#### Ask your agent

- “Draw how a login request travels through our app.”
- “Explain caching on the Lienzo, one Sheet per idea.”

#### Tips

- The canvas never sends anything to the agent. You talk to it in its chat; it reads what you selected.
- Every change can be undone, yours and the agent's.

### Finding your way

Move around, zoom, and fit everything in view.

The canvas is as large as it needs to be. The minimap in the corner shows where you are, and the zoom control fits everything or the selection in view.

Shortcut: ⇧1

#### By hand

1. Scroll to pan, or hold Space and drag.
2. Hold ⌘ (Ctrl on Windows and Linux) and scroll to zoom around the pointer, or pinch on a trackpad.
3. Press Shift+1 to fit everything, Shift+2 to fit the selection, 0 for 100 %.

### Editing in Properties

Everything an agent can set, you can set by hand, without JSON.

Select something and the Properties panel shows its fields: the title, the fields that matter for its kind, and More options for the rest. Lists (checklist items, files, flow events, choices) are edited row by row, words with a known vocabulary are chips, and durations are typed in seconds. Changes save by themselves a moment after you stop typing, each one a step you can undo.

Shortcut: ⌘\

#### By hand

1. Select one thing; the Properties panel opens on the right (⌘\ hides or shows it).
2. Edit a field; it saves 600 ms after the last key. Adding, removing, moving and ticking save at once.
3. Open More options for the less common fields.
4. Press a row of a list to show its tools: move up or down, remove, and for files indent, highlight or mute.
5. Double-click a selected card to rename it on the canvas: Enter saves, Escape keeps the old title.

#### Tips

- If a change is refused, the panel says why under the field and keeps your draft, with Retry.
- Raw data (JSON), at the end, is exactly what the agent reads and writes. You never need it, but it is there.

## Drawing

### Select

Pick things to move, edit or ask about.

Select is the tool you use most. What you select is what the Properties panel shows, what extensions act on, and what your agent reads when you say "this" in your chat.

Shortcut: V

#### By hand

1. Press V, or the arrow in the toolbar.
2. Click a card to select it; Shift-click adds or removes one.
3. Drag on empty canvas to select everything in a box.
4. Drag a selected card to move it; the arrow keys nudge it (with Shift, further).
5. Press Enter or F2 to edit the title of the one selected; Tab moves to the next card.

#### Tips

- ⌘A selects everything; Escape clears the selection.
- Double-click empty canvas to add a card right there.

### Hand

Move the view without moving anything on it.

The Hand moves the camera only, so nothing gets dragged by accident. It is handy on a touch screen and while reading a busy Lienzo.

Shortcut: H

#### By hand

1. Press H, or hold Space for as long as you need it.
2. Drag anywhere to move the view.
3. Press V to go back to Select.

#### Tips

- Moving the view yourself stops following the agent; press F to follow again.

### Pencil

Freehand strokes over the canvas.

The Pencil is for quick marks: circling something, an arrow to a detail, a sketch. Your strokes are solid; strokes the agent draws are dashed and labelled, so you always know who drew what.

Shortcut: P

#### By hand

1. Press P.
2. Draw. Each stroke is kept, simplified, as a drawing you can move and delete.
3. Change the colour and weight in the Pencil options tab of the Properties panel.

#### Ask your agent

- “Circle the part of the diagram where the request can fail.”
- “Underline the two cards I should read first.”

#### Tips

- Lock the tool (the lock in the toolbar) to draw several strokes in a row.
- The Eraser removes whole strokes; Undo brings them back.

### Eraser

Removes whole strokes you drew.

The Eraser removes Pencil strokes one at a time. It never cuts a stroke in half, and Undo brings back anything it removed.

Shortcut: E

#### By hand

1. Press E.
2. Drag over the strokes to remove.
3. The Eraser options can also clear all your own strokes at once.

### Links

Lines between cards and Frames that say how they relate.

A link joins two things and says how they relate: flow (one leads to the next), depends (one needs the other) or reference (one mentions the other). A link is drawn from where the reader starts to where they finish, so link in reading order.

#### By hand

1. Select a card and drag from one of the round handles on its edges onto another card or Frame.
2. Or press a handle once to add a new card already linked on that side.
3. Or select two things and choose Connect the two in ⌘K.
4. Select a link to give it a label, a kind, a colour, or to reverse it.

#### Ask your agent

- “Link the API to the database, labelled "reads".”
- “Join the two Frames with one link instead of the many links between their cards.”

#### Tips

- One link between two Frames reads better than many links between their cards.
- Deleting a card removes its links.

## Shapes

### Shapes

Rectangles, ellipses, diamonds and more, with an optional label.

Shapes are for drawing by hand: boxes, a decision diamond, a database cylinder, a line. Each can carry a label, a stroke, a fill colour and a weight that sets both the outline and the label size.

Shortcut: R

#### By hand

1. Press R for a rectangle or O for an ellipse; the Shape button in the toolbar has the others.
2. Drag to size it. Shift keeps it square or round.
3. Type to give it a label.
4. Change colour, fill and weight in the Properties panel.

#### Ask your agent

- “Draw a diamond for the "is the user signed in?" decision.”
- “Put a red box around the risky part.”

#### Tips

- To explain how things relate, cards and links read better than drawn shapes and arrows: the agent uses them for that.

### Arrows and lines

Straight lines, with or without an arrowhead.

An arrow is a drawn line: it points at something without being a real relation. For a relation the agent can read, use a link.

Shortcut: A

#### By hand

1. Press A for an arrow; the Shape menu also has a plain line.
2. Drag from start to end. Shift snaps to 15°.
3. Choose the heads and the weight in the Properties panel.

### Architecture icons

Icons for systems drawings: servers, databases, users and more.

A small library of icons for drawing systems. Each one is a static SVG image, cleaned on the server, that keeps its attribution and licence.

#### By hand

1. Press + and choose Architecture icons.
2. Click an icon, then click where it goes.
3. Add a caption in the Properties panel.

#### Ask your agent

- “Draw our system with icons: a browser, the API server and a Postgres database.”

### Import SVG

A vector drawing from code, a file or a link.

Bring a vector drawing onto the canvas: paste SVG code, choose a file or give a link. Lienzo keeps only static drawing: scripts, links and outside images are removed.

#### By hand

1. Press + and choose Import SVG….
2. Paste the code, pick a file (up to 64 KB) or give an http(s) link.
3. Place it on the canvas; resize it from its corner.

## Text

### Free text

A label without a card, placed anywhere.

Free text is a label on the canvas or inside a Frame, with no card around it: a heading for an area, a short remark, a caption.

Shortcut: T

#### By hand

1. Press T.
2. Click where the text goes and type.
3. Press Escape when you are done. Change size, font, colour and alignment in the Properties panel.

#### Ask your agent

- “Add a heading "Checkout" above the payment cards.”

### Card

A node: a title, a short summary and optional detail. The agent's main building block.

A card (a node) is one idea: a title, a summary of one to three sentences, and more detail for whoever wants it. Systems, flows and explanations are drawn as cards joined by links and grouped in Frames.

#### By hand

1. Double-click empty canvas, type a title and press Enter.
2. Or press + and choose Node under Blocks.
3. Edit the summary and the detail in the Properties panel; pick a status from its chips (or Other… for your own word).
4. Double-click a selected card to rename it in place.

#### Ask your agent

- “Add a card for the retry queue with a short summary.”
- “Turn this list into cards linked in order.”

#### Tips

- Keep summaries short: a Lienzo is read at a glance. Put the rest in details.

### Note

A paragraph of explanation.

A note holds prose: the why behind a diagram, a caveat, a definition. Use few of them; cards read better than long columns of text.

#### By hand

1. Press + and choose Note under Blocks.
2. Write in the Properties panel, or press Enter to edit it on the canvas.

#### Ask your agent

- “Add a short note explaining why we cache at the edge.”

### Code

Example code, highlighted. It does not run.

A code block shows a snippet with its language: a request, a config, a function. It never runs. For something you can try, ask for a mini app.

#### By hand

1. Press + and choose Code under Blocks.
2. Paste the code and set the language in the Properties panel.

#### Ask your agent

- “Show the fetch call that sends the token, as a code block.”

## Frames

### Frame

A frame that holds things together.

A Frame groups cards, drawings and other Frames into one area with a title and a purpose: Client and Server, Before and After. Frames nest up to four deep, move as one, and can carry their own instructions for the agent.

Shortcut: M

#### By hand

1. Press M to add an empty Frame, then drag things into it.
2. Or select things and press ⌘G to wrap them in a Frame.
3. Give it a title and a purpose in the Properties panel.
4. Select a Frame and press ⌘⇧G to unwrap it: its contents stay.

#### Ask your agent

- “Group the client cards in a Frame called Browser.”
- “Split this diagram into three Frames: input, processing, output.”

#### Tips

- Aim for about nine cards per Frame; link whole Frames rather than many cards across them.

### Frame layouts

Let a Frame arrange its contents: graph, grid, stack, flow or free.

A Frame can lay out what it holds. Graph follows the links (down or to the right), grid makes columns, stack and flow line things up, and free leaves everything where you put it.

Shortcut: ⌘G

#### By hand

1. Select a Frame.
2. In the Properties panel, open Layout and choose a mode and a direction.
3. Moving a card yourself in a free layout keeps it there.

#### Ask your agent

- “Lay out the Server Frame as a graph going right.”

## Sheets

### Sheets

One chapter per explanation, side by side.

A Sheet is a chapter the agent adds while explaining. Each new explanation gets its own Sheet, placed on one strip from left to right, so a long conversation stays readable. The pill at the top says where you are: Sheet 2 of 3.

Shortcut: ]

#### By hand

1. Press ] for the next Sheet and [ for the previous one.
2. Press ⌘J, or the pill at the top, to jump to any Sheet.
3. Sheets are listed in ⌘K too.

#### Ask your agent

- “Start a new Sheet for the deployment part.”
- “Go back to the Sheet about caching and add the failure case.”

### Following the agent

The camera goes wherever the agent draws.

While the magnet is on, each change the agent makes flies the camera there and glows for a moment. Move the view yourself and it lets go; the agent's next change then shows as a pill above the toolbar.

Shortcut: F

#### By hand

1. Press F, or the magnet next to the Sheet pill, to follow or stop.
2. Press G, or the pill, to go to the agent's latest change and follow again.

## Windows & media

### Window

A window onto a live web page.

A Window shows a web page on the canvas: your app running locally, a doc, a design. It is drawn as a window with a bar you drag it by, and a button to open the page outside the Lienzo.

Shortcut: W

#### By hand

1. Press W.
2. Give the address of the page.
3. Double-click the Window to use the page; Escape gives the canvas back.

#### Ask your agent

- “Show the app on localhost:5173 in a Window next to the diagram.”

#### Tips

- Some sites refuse to be shown inside another page; the Window then offers to open them outside.

### Image, video and audio

A picture, a video or a sound from a link.

Media shows an image, plays a video (a file, YouTube or Vimeo) or a sound from an http(s) link, with an optional caption. Videos never play by themselves.

#### By hand

1. Press + and choose Image, Video or Audio under Embeds.
2. Paste the link and an optional caption.
3. Double-click an image to see it full size.

#### Ask your agent

- “Put the architecture diagram from this link on the Lienzo as an image.”

## Interactive blocks

### Controls

Sliders, switches and choices for values shared by a Frame or the whole Lienzo.

Controls turn a question into something you can try: up to four variables (numbers as sliders, on/off switches, choices), shared with the other blocks of the same Frame or Lienzo. Your agent reads where you left them and which one you moved last.

#### By hand

1. Press + and choose Controls under Blocks; write its question in Properties.
2. Under Variables shown, press Show a variable… to pick one the block can reach, or New variable to make one: a label, a type, and whether this Frame or the whole Lienzo shares it.
3. Open a variable's row to change its range, unit or choices; move rows up or down, or stop showing one.
4. Use the controls on the canvas. Reset puts them back.

#### Ask your agent

- “Add controls for interest rate and years, and a card that explains the result.”
- “Look at where I left the sliders and tell me what that means.”

### Variables

Named values a Frame or the Lienzo shares: numbers, on/off, choices.

A variable is a value the blocks of a Frame (or the whole Lienzo) share: Controls show it, shaders and other blocks read it, and your agent sees where you left it. Each one has a label, a type (Number, On / off or Choice), where it starts, and a name in code that is filled in from the label.

#### By hand

1. Select a Frame, or nothing for the Lienzo (with the panel pinned), and open Variables in Properties.
2. Press Number, On / off or Choice to add one.
3. Open its row: set Lowest, Highest, Step, Unit and Starts at for a number, Starts on for a switch, or the list of choices.
4. When a control has moved it, the row says Now at … with Back to start.
5. Renaming or deleting a variable updates the Controls that show it.

#### Ask your agent

- “Add a variable for gravity from 0 to 20 m/s² on this Frame and show it in the controls.”
- “Make the speed variable a choice between slow, normal and fast.”

### Animated flow

Time and cause travelling along the real links of the Lienzo.

An animated flow plays events over the links already on the canvas: a request going out, a value coming back, a retry. It shows order and timing that a still diagram cannot.

#### By hand

1. Your agent usually builds it from the links on the canvas; you can also add Animated flow from the + catalog.
2. In Properties, add events row by row: pick the link or the two ends from a list, what travels, and when (in seconds).
3. Set the duration with its slider, in seconds.
4. Press play to run it; step through it, or scrub along its timeline.

#### Ask your agent

- “Animate a request travelling from the browser to the database and back.”
- “Show what happens over time when the cache misses.”

### GLSL shader

An image computed from a few parameters, live.

A shader draws a picture from code and a few sliders, so you can see what each parameter does. It runs with WebGL on the web and desktop and shows a still reference on the phone.

#### By hand

1. Your agent usually writes the shader; you can edit its code in Properties.
2. Add, rename or remove parameters as rows: the code's declarations follow. Use a shared variable to bind one to a Frame's variable.
3. Tick resolution or time when the code uses them.
4. Move the sliders; press play when it uses time.

#### Ask your agent

- “Show me how a sine wave changes with frequency, as a shader with a slider.”

### File tree

Folders and files with a short note each. Folders open and close.

A file tree shows the structure of a project with a few words about each entry, the important ones highlighted. Folders open and close.

#### By hand

1. Press + and choose File tree under Embeds.
2. In Properties, add files and folders row by row; select a row to indent or outdent it, write its note, highlight or mute it, or make a folder start closed.
3. Open and close folders on the canvas.

#### Ask your agent

- “Draw the folders of this repository and mark the three files I should read first.”

### Checklist

Steps to go through and tick.

A checklist is a short list of steps you tick as you go. Your agent can read what you ticked.

#### By hand

1. Press + and choose Checklist under Blocks.
2. Select it and type in the + Add an item row at its end, then press Enter; or add, reorder and remove items in Properties.
3. Tick them on the canvas.

#### Ask your agent

- “Make a checklist for releasing the app.”

## Mini apps

### Mini app

A small HTML, CSS and JavaScript page, alive inside the Lienzo.

When something is better understood by using it than by reading about it (an algorithm, a layout, a state machine, a formula), your agent can build it as a mini app: a complete page in a Window on the canvas. It runs sandboxed, with no access to the canvas page.

#### By hand

1. Press + and choose Mini app under Embeds for a starting page.
2. Double-click it to use it; Escape gives the canvas back.
3. Edit its HTML in the Properties panel.

#### Ask your agent

- “Build a mini app where I can step through binary search on a list.”
- “Make a little simulator for this queue: I add jobs and watch them drain.”

#### Tips

- For a project with several files or a server, ask for a Window on the running app instead.

### Mini apps that remember

What you did in a mini app stays on its block, for you and your agent.

A mini app can store a small result on its block: your answer, a choice, a step reached. It comes back when the page opens again, and your agent reads it. Nothing is sent to the agent: you tell it in your chat, and it looks.

#### By hand

1. Use the mini app.
2. In your chat, say what you did: "I tried the mini app, look at my answer."

#### Ask your agent

- “Make the quiz mini app remember my answers.”
- “Read what I left in the mini app and tell me what I got wrong.”

## Lenses

### Lenses

A way to colour the same canvas.

A Lens keeps every card where it is and tints it by something the canvas does not show: who changed it last, how long ago, or whether you changed it since the agent did. The legend says what each colour means.

Shortcut: L

#### By hand

1. Press L, or the Lens control above the minimap, to go to the next Lens.
2. Press it until it says No Lens to turn it off.

#### Tips

- Lenses read the stored history, the 50 most recent changes, and say so.

### Who changed it

Your changes in the accent, the agent's in violet.

Shows who last changed each card: you (accent), the agent (violet), or nobody recently (neutral). Useful after the agent has worked for a while.

Shortcut: L

### How fresh

What just changed, what is recent, what has settled.

Tints each card by how long it has been left alone: just changed, recent, settled, or still. It shows at a glance where the work is happening.

Shortcut: L

### The agent's version

Where you changed things after the agent did.

Shows where each card stands against the agent's last edit: as the agent left it, changed by you since, or not touched by the agent. Before asking the agent to continue, it shows what it has not seen you change.

Shortcut: L

## Shortcuts

### Keyboard shortcuts

Every key, and how to change it.

Almost everything has a key. The list below is the one in use now, with your changes. Change any of them in Settings → Shortcuts: press the key chip, then the new keys.

Shortcut: ?

#### By hand

1. Press ? to open Settings → Shortcuts.
2. Press a key chip and then the new keys; Escape cancels.
3. Keys another shortcut held move to the new one, and the other shows a warning.

### Command palette

Search every tool, action, Sheet, Lienzo and Help page.

⌘K (Ctrl+K) opens one search over everything Lienzo can do: tools, actions on the selection, Sheets, your Lienzos, extensions, settings and these Help pages. The keyboard alone is enough.

Shortcut: ⌘K

#### By hand

1. Press ⌘K, or the search button at the top right.
2. Type a few letters; arrows move, Enter runs.
3. ⌘Enter runs and keeps the palette open.

### Pinned tools

Your favourite tools in the toolbar, on keys 1 to 9.

Pin any tool, block or extension from the + catalog to the toolbar. Pinned tools get the keys 1 to 9 in order.

#### By hand

1. Press + and hover a row; press its pin.
2. Reorder or unpin them in Settings → Toolbar.

### Hide all UI

Only the canvas, for reading or presenting.

Hides the toolbar, the panels and the islands so only the Lienzo shows. Failures and the zoom stay visible.

Shortcut: ⌘.

#### By hand

1. Press ⌘. or choose Hide all UI in the menu.
2. Press it again, or Escape, to bring everything back.

## Agents

### Connect an agent

Give your agent the canvas tools once.

Your agent draws through a small set of canvas tools. In Paseo they are there for every agent. In the desktop app, Settings → Agents shows the address and the one command to add them to Claude Code, Codex or Cursor; the agents that connected are listed there.

#### By hand

1. Desktop: open Settings → Agents and copy the command for your agent.
2. Run it once in a terminal, then restart the agent.
3. Paseo: nothing to set up; open a conversation next to the Lienzo.

#### Ask your agent

- “List my Lienzos.”
- “Open the Lienzo about sign-in and add the logout flow.”

### Drawing while it works

Turn on the copilot and the agent sketches as it answers.

In Paseo, the Lienzo chip under the message box turns the copilot on for that conversation: the agent then draws what it explains as it thinks, after each step, once per task, or by your own rule. It starts off; with it off, the agent draws only when you ask.

#### By hand

1. In a Paseo conversation, press the Lienzo chip under the message box.
2. Choose when the agent draws.
3. Watch the Lienzo: the magnet follows the agent while it draws.

#### Ask your agent

- “Draw as you go while you investigate this bug.”

#### Tips

- In the desktop app, ask the agent to draw in its own chat; the canvas follows it the same way.

### Point and ask

Select something, then ask about "this" in your own chat.

The canvas never talks to the agent: your chat does. Select a card, a Frame or a few things, then say "look at this" in your conversation. The agent reads what you selected, its instructions, and what you did with it (sliders, a quiz answer, a mini app's result).

#### By hand

1. Select what you mean on the canvas.
2. In your chat, refer to it: "this", "these", "what I selected".
3. The agent answers in the chat and may draw on the Lienzo.

#### Ask your agent

- “Look at this and explain it more simply.”
- “What is wrong with the cards I selected?”
- “Expand this Frame into its own Sheet.”

### Instructions for the agent

Tell the agent how to explain, on a Lienzo, a Frame or a card.

Instructions say how the agent should work here: for whom it explains, what to focus on, what to avoid. They can be set on the whole Lienzo, on a Frame or on one card; the most specific one wins, and the agent reads them with the selection.

#### By hand

1. For the Lienzo: menu → Instructions for the agent.
2. For a Frame or a card: select it and open Instructions for the agent in the Properties panel.
3. Write a sentence or two; it saves when you leave the field.

#### Ask your agent

- “Read the instructions on this Frame and follow them.”

### History and undo

Every change, yours and the agent's, by day.

Every change is a step you can undo: ⌘Z and ⌘⇧Z. History lists the steps by day with who made them; pressing a chip flies to what changed. The agent can undo only its own latest step, never yours.

Shortcut: ⌘Z

#### By hand

1. Press ⌘Z to undo, ⌘⇧Z to redo.
2. Open History from the menu to see every step.

#### Ask your agent

- “Undo your last change on the Lienzo.”

## Extensions

### What extensions are

Small tools you or your agent add to Lienzo.

An extension is a small tool written as one HTML page. It opens as a tab of the Properties panel and works on the selection: count things, tidy titles, show the Lienzo another way. Extensions work in Paseo and the desktop app, on the web and desktop. Each installed one with its own guide has a page in this section.

#### By hand

1. Open Extensions from the menu, or Manage extensions… in the + catalog.
2. Open a tool from the + catalog, under Extensions.

#### Ask your agent

- “Make me a Lienzo tool that…”
- “Which extensions do I have installed?”

### Add from a file

Install an extension someone sent you, after a review.

An extension file is JSON. Add from file… reads it and shows a review before anything is saved: what each extension does, what it asks for, and whether it is new or replaces one. Nothing runs until you press Install, and it holds no permission until you allow it.

#### By hand

1. Open Extensions and press Add from file….
2. Choose the .json file.
3. Read the review, then press Install.

### Discover

Extensions others published, ready to install.

Discover lists the extensions in the Lienzo extensions catalog, a public repository on GitHub. Installing one fetches its file and shows the same review as a file you add yourself. The list is kept for when you are offline.

#### By hand

1. Open Extensions and choose Discover.
2. Press Install on a card.
3. Read the review, then press Install again.

#### Tips

- Without a connection, Discover shows the last list it read and says when.

### Permissions

What an extension may do, and how to allow it.

Every extension runs in its own sandboxed frame, with no access to Paseo, the plugin, your files or other sites. Reading the Lienzo and selecting are always allowed. Changing the canvas (edit) and loading from the internet (network) are asked for. Extensions from a file or from Discover hold nothing until you press Allow.

#### By hand

1. Open Extensions.
2. A waiting card says what it asks for; press Allow to grant it.
3. Remove an extension to take everything back.

### Export and share

One extension as its own file, or all of yours in one.

Export on an extension's card saves it as a single-extension file anyone can add with Add from file…. Export all mine saves every extension made here, by you or your agent, in one file.

#### By hand

1. Open Extensions.
2. Press Export on a card, or Export all mine at the top.

### Publish to the catalog

Propose your extension to everyone with a GitHub pull request.

Publish… on an extension you made checks it, saves its file and opens GitHub in your browser to propose it to the catalog. Lienzo never asks for a GitHub token. When the catalog's checks pass and the pull request is merged, the extension appears in Discover for everyone.

#### By hand

1. Open Extensions and press Publish… on your extension's card.
2. Lienzo checks it and saves the file.
3. Press Open GitHub: sign in, add the file at the path shown, and open the pull request.

#### Tips

- Give it a clear name, a one-line description and a short Help page: they become its card in Discover.

## Make your own

### Make your own

Ask your agent for a tool, try it, and share it. No build step.

An extension is a small tool that joins Lienzo: one HTML page that reads the Lienzo, changes the selection and, with your permission, edits the canvas in one undoable step. You do not need to write it yourself: your agent writes it, saves it, and it appears in the + catalog. These pages walk through it from the first request to sharing it in the catalog.

#### By hand

1. Ask your agent for the tool (step 1).
2. Read what it saved in Extensions (step 2).
3. Open it from the + catalog and try it on a few cards (step 3).
4. Check what it may do (step 4).
5. Export it or publish it to the catalog (step 5).

#### Ask your agent

- “Make me a Lienzo extension that counts the cards in the selection.”
- “Write a Lienzo tool that turns the selected cards into a checklist.”

### 1. Ask your agent

Say what the tool is for, what it acts on, and what it changes.

Your agent saves extensions with the canvas_catalog tool, which asks for your approval the first time. A good request says three things: what the tool works on (the selection, a Frame, the whole Lienzo), what it shows, and what it changes when you press it.

#### By hand

1. Open the conversation where your agent works (in Paseo, the chat next to the Lienzo; on desktop, the agent's own app or terminal).
2. Describe the tool in one or two sentences.
3. Approve the catalog change when your agent asks.

#### Ask your agent

- “Make a Lienzo extension called Title Case: it shows how many cards are selected and has one button that rewrites their titles in Title Case.”
- “Write a Lienzo tool that shows the selected Frame's cards as a numbered list I can copy.”
- “Add a page of Help to your extension that explains how to use it.”

#### Tips

- Ask for a Help page too: the agent adds a docs field and the tool gets its own page here, under Extensions.
- Name the permission it may need. A tool that only reads and selects needs none.

### 2. What it writes

A manifest and one self-contained page that talks to window.lienzo.

Your agent saves a manifest: an id, a name, a one-line description, an icon, the permissions it asks for, the page (html), and optionally its Help page (docs, short Markdown). The page runs sandboxed in its own frame, with no access to Paseo, your files or other sites. It reaches the canvas only through window.lienzo.

#### The parts of the page
- `lienzo.onContext(fn)` calls `fn` with the Lienzo (cards, Frames, links, where each one is), the selection and the theme's colours, now and on every change.
- `lienzo.select(ids)` changes the selection; `lienzo.open(id)` goes to a card on the canvas.
- `lienzo.edit(operations, label)` changes the canvas in one transaction you can undo. It needs the **edit** permission.
- `lienzo.kit.stage(...)` draws things with the canvas' own selection, hover and drag behaviour.

#### The manifest
```json
{
  "id": "title-case",
  "kind": "tool",
  "api": 1,
  "name": "Title Case",
  "description": "Gives the selected cards titles in Title Case.",
  "icon": "CaseSensitive",
  "permissions": [
    "edit"
  ],
  "html": "<p id=\"info\">…</p><script>…</script>",
  "docs": "Title Case gives every selected card…"
}
```

The whole contract is in [docs/extensions.md](https://github.com/Gabsplat/paseo-canvas/blob/master/docs/extensions.md).

### 3. Test it

Open it from the + catalog and try it on a few cards.

A saved extension appears at once in the + catalog under Extensions, in ⌘K, and as a card in the Extensions screen. It opens as a tab of the Properties panel and works on the shared selection, so what you select on the canvas is what it sees.

#### By hand

1. Press + in the toolbar and choose your tool under Extensions.
2. Select a few cards: the tool should react at once.
3. Press its button. If it changed the canvas, ⌘Z undoes the whole step.
4. Ask your agent to fix anything that is off; saving the same id replaces the tool.

#### Ask your agent

- “The Title Case tool ignores Frames. Make it rename the selected Frames too.”
- “Your tool's text is hard to read in the light theme. Use the theme colours it is given.”

#### Tips

- Extensions run in the web and desktop apps, not on the phone.
- If the tool says it has no permission, see step 4.

### 4. Permissions

Reading and selecting are free; changing the canvas and the internet are asked for.

An extension declares what it needs: edit (change the canvas) and network (load things from the internet). Without network it can load nothing from outside its own page. A tool made here by you or your agent holds what it declares. One that arrives in a file or from the catalog holds nothing until you allow it: until then it can only read and select.

#### By hand

1. Open Extensions (menu → Extensions).
2. A card that waits shows a warning strip: read what it asks for, then press Allow.
3. Replacing the file with different code asks again.

#### Tips

- There is no permission to talk to the agent: the canvas never sends anything to it. You talk to your agent in your own chat.

### 5. Share it

Export one file, or publish it to the catalog with a pull request.

Every extension travels as an extension file (JSON). Export saves one tool as its own file: send it to someone and they add it with Add from file…, after a review of what it asks for. To share it with everyone, Publish… checks it, saves the file, and opens GitHub to propose it to the Lienzo extensions catalog. Once the pull request is merged it shows in Discover.

#### By hand

1. Open Extensions and find your tool's card.
2. Press Export for a file, or Publish… for the catalog.
3. Publish… checks the tool, saves the file and opens GitHub. Sign in there, add the file, and open the pull request.
4. Add a README.md and a screenshot.png next to extension.json if you like.

#### Tips

- Lienzo never holds a GitHub token: everything on GitHub happens in your browser.
- Every id in a file starts with the file's id and a dot, like title-case.title-case.

### A complete example

Title Case: the whole extension, ready to save or import.

This is a complete, small extension. It reads the selection, shows how many cards are selected, and rewrites their titles in one undoable step. It uses the theme's colours so it reads well in light and dark, and it brings its own Help page.

#### Ask your agent

- “Save the Title Case example from Lienzo Help as an extension.”

#### The page (html)
```html
<style>body{margin:0;padding:12px;font:13px system-ui,sans-serif}button{font:inherit;padding:6px 12px;border-radius:6px;border:1px solid;cursor:pointer}button:disabled{opacity:.5;cursor:default}</style>
<p id="info">Select some cards.</p>
<button id="go" disabled>Title Case the titles</button>
<script>
var ctx = null, info = document.getElementById('info'), go = document.getElementById('go');
function chosen() { return ctx ? ctx.document.blocks.filter(function (b) { return ctx.selection.indexOf(b.id) >= 0; }) : []; }
function titleCase(t) { return t.replace(/\b\w/g, function (c) { return c.toUpperCase(); }); }
lienzo.onContext(function (c) {
  ctx = c; var k = c.theme.colors, n = chosen().length;
  document.body.style.background = k.surface; document.body.style.color = k.foreground;
  go.style.background = k.accent; go.style.color = k.background; go.style.borderColor = k.accent;
  info.textContent = n ? n + ' selected' : 'Select some cards.';
  go.disabled = !n;
});
go.onclick = function () {
  var ops = chosen().slice(0, 200).map(function (b) { return { type: 'block.update', id: b.id, patch: { title: titleCase(b.title) } }; });
  lienzo.edit(ops, 'Title Case').then(function () { info.textContent = 'Done. Undo brings the old titles back.'; }, function (e) { info.textContent = e.message; });
};
</script>
```

#### The file to share
Export writes the extension inside the file container. Its id is the file's id and a dot:
```json
{
  "format": "paseo-canvas-pack",
  "version": 1,
  "id": "title-case",
  "name": "Title Case",
  "description": "Gives the selected cards titles in Title Case.",
  "blockTypes": [],
  "templates": [],
  "documents": [],
  "extensions": [
    {
      "id": "title-case.title-case",
      "kind": "tool",
      "api": 1,
      "name": "Title Case",
      "description": "Gives the selected cards titles in Title Case.",
      "icon": "CaseSensitive",
      "permissions": [
        "edit"
      ],
      "html": "…the page above…",
      "docs": "…its Help page…"
    }
  ]
}
```
